Q: How can I specify the Python version used to create a virtual environment? A:

Assuming that you have installed python3 or any desired version of Python (2.6, 2.7, 3.5, 3.6), now while creating the virtual environment, directly pass the Python executable path. Hence here are few valid examples:

virtualenv new_p2_env # Creates a new default Python environment (usually Python 2)

virtualenv -p python3 new_p3_env # Creates a new default python3 ('python3' must be a valid command, i.e., found in the PATH)

And last

# Directly point to any version of the Python interpreter binary. This can even be another virtualenv's

'bin/python'. virtualenv -p /path/to/any/bin/python new_env

Q: Where does python handle modular calculations differently? A:

If you want to use modular arithmetic to perform division by 2, why not use the modular inverse of 2 modulo 63799, i.e. pow(2, -1, 63799) == 31900, instead of 63799 // 2 == 31899:

n = 63799
inv2 = pow(2, -1, n)  # 31900
db = []
d = 977
db.append(d)
for i in range(5):
    d &= -2  # minus 1 from `d` if `d` is odd, to make the division a floor division
    d = (d * inv2) % n
    db.append(d)

print(db)  # [977, 488, 244, 122, 61, 30]

Q: Do I need to create an abstract method for toString and equals? A:

You do not need to declare equals(Object) and toString() as abstract methods in the parent class, since these methods are already declared and implemented in Object and every class (but Object itself) inherits from Object.

You can declare equals(Object) and toString() as abstract in the parent class to force every (non-abstract) subclass to implement these methods and not use the inherited methods (from Object or any other parent.)

Q: Open external website inside Acumatica popup without exposing URL in browser A:

What you’re running into is basically a limitation of how Acumatica handles navigation vs. what the browser will always expose.

Even if you open a PX popup or a new window, the moment you navigate directly to an external URL, the browser will show it. There’s no supported Acumatica mechanism that “hides” a real external URL from the address bar once you leave the Acumatica domain.

What you can do in Acumatica

Since your external app supports iframe embedding, the cleanest Acumatica-friendly approach is:

1. Use a custom Acumatica screen with an iframe container

Instead of redirecting, create a custom graph + ASPX screen (or a simplified custom page) that renders an iframe, and load your external app inside it.

So your Acumatica action would open something like:

~/Pages/Custom/ExternalPortal.aspx?sessionId=xyz

And inside that page:

<iframe 
    src="https://externalapp.com/?s=...&u=...&c=...&corp=..."
    style="width:100%; height:100vh; border:none;">
</iframe>

From the user’s perspective:

  • They stay inside Acumatica UI

  • The browser URL stays on your Acumatica domain

  • The external app is embedded inside the frame

2. Open it as an Acumatica popup (PXSmartPanel)

You can also host the iframe inside a PXSmartPanel if you want it modal-like:

  • Create a SmartPanel

  • Put an iframe inside it

  • Load the URL dynamically via PXDataSource / parameters

This gives you the “popup inside Acumatica” experience you’re describing.

3. What you cannot do (important)

  • You cannot open a true external URL in a new tab/window and hide it

  • You cannot prevent the browser address bar from showing the external domain if you navigate there directly

  • PXRedirectToUrlException will always expose the final URL

Important caveat (this is usually the gotcha)

Even if iframe embedding is allowed by the external app:

  • You must ensure it does NOT send X-Frame-Options: DENY/SAMEORIGIN

  • You may need CSP headers configured properly

  • Session handling in query strings inside iframes can sometimes break due to browser privacy rules (especially third-party cookie restrictions)

Recommended architecture (what most Acumatica integrations do)

The most stable pattern is:

Acumatica screen → internal “wrapper page” → iframe → external app

This avoids exposing the external URL in navigation and keeps Acumatica in control of UI flow.

Q: django admin action without selecting objects A:

I found a simple solution modifying the action form.

Django uses _selected_action to get the selected objects by the user, if no items selected a validation error will be thrown.

We can bypass this validation by adding a default value in _selecte_action field, this way Django thinks the user selected one object and runs the action.

EmptyActionForm behavior: If no actions are selected, the action will receive an empty queryset, otherwise the action will receive a queryset with the selected objects.

from django import forms
from django.contrib import admin
from django.contrib.admin.helpers import ActionForm


class EmptyActionForm(ActionForm):

    _selected_action = forms.BooleanField(
        label="",
        required=False,
        initial=1,
        widget=forms.HiddenInput(),
    )


@admin.register(Book)
class BookModelAdmin(admin.ModelAdmin):
    # ...
    action_form = EmptyActionForm
    # ...

Note: This works for me using Django 5.2, I'dont know if this solution works with older versions.

Edit: By default Django hides the actions if there are no registries in the admin, to prevent this you can modify the change list instance and set show_admin_actions to True.

@admin.register(Book)
class BookModelAdmin(admin.ModelAdmin):
    # ...

    action_form = EmptyActionForm

    def get_changelist_instance(self, request):
        change_list = super().get_changelist_instance(request)
        change_list.show_admin_actions = True
        return change_list
